name: dbacl
why: Digram-based Bayesian text classifier from the early days of spam filtering; old-school and uncommon, though mostly a classic utility.

brief.what_it_is: dbacl is a set of lightweight UNIX/POSIX command-line utilities that classify text documents using Bayesian statistics. You train it on example document collections, and it computes the posterior probability that a new text resembles each one, then makes a decision based on misclassification costs you choose. The executables listed are bayesol, dbacl, hmine, hypex, mailcross, mailfoot, mailinspect and mailtoe. dbacl is also the name of the core utility. The homepage does not describe the exact input and output formats.
brief.why_it_exists: The author presents it as a simple, powerful, easily integrated set of tools for automatic text classification. The homepage lists uses such as junk email filtering, web page screening, automated answering machines, email prioritization, topical news gathering, and even playing chess.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage says dbacl computes posterior probabilities with Bayesian methods, combining prior beliefs with observed text, and then chooses the mathematically optimal class under arbitrary misclassification costs. The name suggests a digram (two-character sequence) model, but the homepage does not spell out the mechanism. The tutorial and man page are linked from the homepage, but I could not get their addresses from the fetched text.
brief.install_notes: The homepage has a Download link and a CVS link, but I did not follow them. Nothing about dependencies, configuration, or first-run steps appeared on the homepage. The brew formula lists eight executables.
brief.standout: Unlike most spam filters of its era, it is a set of small Unix tools meant to be composed in shell scripts, not a single application. Its digram-based Bayesian approach is a classic early-spam-era design.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage shows no release date, last-commit date, or changelog, and the scout note calls it old-school and uncommon. Links to Forums and CVS suggest an older SourceForge-era project, but I could not confirm whether it is still maintained.
brief.caveats: The homepage is the only page I could read, and it is thin on specifics. It gives no commands, install steps, platform list, or benchmarks. The Brew formula has no caveats. The homepage says the project is GPL-licensed Free Software. The page links to CVS, which suggests an older source-control setup.
quotes: The dbacl project consist of a set of lightweight UNIX/POSIX utilities which can be used, either directly or in shell scripts, to classify text documents automatically, according to Bayesian statistical principles.
The dbacl utilities cannot do all these tasks directly, but by concentrating on simple, powerful, and easily integrated tools these applications become possible.
The dbacl utilities are Free Software distributed under the terms of the GNU General Public License (GPL).

judge.reason: A small Unix text classifier built around digramic Bayesian modeling and configurable misclassification costs offers a distinctive, hands-on glimpse of statistical decision theory.

entry.title: dbacl
entry.tldr: A set of small Unix tools that learn from example text and then say which category a new document most resembles, using Bayesian statistics.
entry.deeper_look:
dbacl is a collection of command-line utilities for classifying text. You give it collections of example documents, one per category. It learns a model of each, then computes the probability that a new piece of text belongs to each category. The decision step can weigh the cost of different mistakes, so a wrongly discarded email can count for more than a wrongly kept one.

The homepage lists uses such as junk email filtering, web page screening, automated answering machines, email prioritization, topical news gathering, and even playing chess. The author is candid that the tools do not do all of this directly: "by concentrating on simple, powerful, and easily integrated tools these applications become possible." The pieces are meant to be glued together in shell scripts.

The idea underneath is a door into statistical text classification, the same family of techniques behind early spam filters. You combine prior beliefs with observed text and choose the class that minimizes expected cost. The name suggests a digram model, meaning two-character sequences, but the homepage does not spell out the mechanism. Reading the man page and tutorial is where the details would be.

The formula installs eight executables: bayesol, dbacl, hmine, hypex, mailcross, mailfoot, mailinspect and mailtoe. dbacl is the core, and the mail* names point at email-oriented helpers. The homepage does not describe the other tools in detail.

Shows the options of the decision tool, which applies misclassification costs to pick a class.
Shows what the mail inspection helper expects, as a hint of how the tools are meant to work on email.

entry.whats_unique: Most spam filters of its era were single applications. dbacl is a set of small composable Unix tools with a cost-aware decision step, built for shell scripts.
entry.caveats: Maintenance status is unknown, the homepage shows no release dates and links to CVS, and it gives no example commands, so expect to read the man page.
